html:
The Leco are a people of the eastern Andes foothills of Bolivia, north of La Paz, around Apolo, Guanay and the Mapiri and Kaka rivers. Their language is an isolate, now almost lost, though several thousand people count themselves Leco.

The foothills linked the highland world of the Inca with the Amazon lowlands, and the Leco lived on that edge, trading with highland peoples such as the Kallawaya. Missionaries worked among them from the 1600s, and gold mining and rubber collecting later drew outsiders to their rivers. Neighbours: Tacana and Mosetén.
